outcome: C. albicans oral colonization in infants
cohort: The cohort consisted of 160 mother-child dyads from whom oral samples were collected during pregnancy and up to two years postpartum.
finding: The study found that 94% of mother-child dyads with oral C. albicans had highly genetically related strains, and mothers with higher dental plaque accumulation (plaque index >=2) had an 8.02 times increased risk of vertically transmitting C. albicans to their infants.
mod_finding: Delivery method did not show a significant association with C. albicans vertical transmission.
